deep.reconstruction:
Problem 60 (Opera Postuma I, 'Fragmenta ex Adversariis', arithmetic). A right triangle with generators (p,q) has area A = pq(p^2-q^2) = pq(p-q)(p+q). A second triangle with generators (r,s) has area B = rs(r-s)(r+s). The task is to make A/B = a/b for a given ratio a:b. Euler says a direct general treatment fails. He therefore gives particular solutions by one device: choose r and s as simple linear forms in p and q so that three of the four factors of B coincide with factors of A (up to constants). A/B then collapses to a ratio of two linear forms in p and q. Setting this equal to a/b gives p/q as a linear-fractional function of a and b.

Case I. Take r = p, s = p-q. Then r+s = 2p-q and r-s = q, so B = p(p-q)(2p-q)q. Hence A/B = (p+q)/(2p-q) = a/b. This gives bp+bq = 2ap-aq, i.e. p(2a-b) = q(a+b). Result: p = a+b, q = 2a-b, r = a+b, s = 2b-a.

Case II. Take r = 2p, s = p+q. Then r+s = 3p+q, r-s = p-q and B = 2p(p+q)(3p+q)(p-q). Hence A/B = q/(6p+2q) = a/b, so bq = 6ap+2aq and p/q = (b-2a)/(6a). Result: p = b-2a, q = 6a, r = 2b-4a, s = b+4a.

Case III. Take r = 2p, s = p-q. Then r+s = 3p-q, r-s = p+q and A/B = q/(6p-2q). From bq = 6ap-2aq, p/q = (b+2a)/(6a). Result: p = b+2a, q = 6a, r = 2b+4a, s = b-4a.

Case IV. Take r = p+q, s = p. Then r+s = 2p+q, r-s = q and A/B = (p-q)/(2p+q). From bp-bq = 2ap+aq, p/q = (a+b)/(b-2a). Result: p = a+b, q = b-2a, r = 2b-a, s = a+b.

Case V. Take r = p+q, s = q. Then r+s = p+2q, r-s = p and A/B = (p-q)/(p+2q). From bp-bq = ap+2aq, p/q = (2a+b)/(b-a). Result: p = 2a+b, q = b-a, r = a+2b, s = b-a.

Case VI. Take r = p+q, s = 2q. Then r+s = p+3q, r-s = p-q and A/B = p/(2p+6q). From bp = 2ap+6aq, p/q = 6a/(b-2a). Result: p = 6a, q = b-2a, r = 4a+b, s = 2b-4a.

Case VII. Take r = p-q, s = q. Then r+s = p, r-s = p-2q and A/B = (p+q)/(p-2q). From bp+bq = ap-2aq, p/q = (b+2a)/(a-b). Result: p = b+2a, q = a-b, r = 2b+a, s = a-b.

Cases VIII-X follow on the next page, followed by a table. There Euler notes that negative generators may be made positive by assigning the larger value to p (or r). Examples follow, e.g. a = b = 1 gives (6,1) and (5,2).

In every case the values of r and s are obtained by substituting p and q into the chosen linear forms (my verification). An overall scaling of p and q is irrelevant, because A/B is homogeneous of degree 0.
errors: No algebraic errors on this page. Every case I-VII checks: each stated r,s substitution, each factor of B, each reduced ratio A/B, each solution for p/q, and each final quadruple (p,q,r,s).

Not an error but unstated: the solutions degenerate in special cases. For example, a = b makes q = 0 in V and VII; b = 2a makes q = 0 in II, IV and VI; a = b gives identical triangles in I. Euler only addresses sign issues (on the next page) and similar-triangle duplicates (in the examples).

results.what: Ten (here seven) linear parametric families of pairs of Pythagorean triangles whose areas stand in an arbitrary prescribed rational ratio a:b. They are obtained by choosing generators (r,s) as linear forms in (p,q) that share three of the four area factors.
results.modern_name: Parametric solutions of the Diophantine equation b*pq(p^2-q^2) = a*rs(r^2-s^2), i.e. pairs of rational right triangles (congruent-number type curves) with areas in given ratio; essentially a factor-matching trick yielding rational points.
results.usually_credited_to: The problem type goes back to Diophantus and to Fermat/Frenicle-era work on right triangles. These particular parametrizations appear in Euler's posthumous Fragmenta (Opera Postuma, 1862).

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary factor-cancellation parametrizations, already published in Euler's Opera Postuma (1862). The material is routine for Euler and for the 18th-century theory of rational right triangles.
